what_happened: The the person running Athena lifted the scope pause on line f5qm (A6). Two attempts had produced no candidate. Job tw3v's plan was 17 steps, then 16 at round 3, and it still failed planning. Spend was $6.72 against a p90 forecast of $3.20. The failures were about plan size and an open design ruling on records, not a wrong goal. A6 is on the speed path and blocks A7-A9. So the the person running Athena split the line by hand into three requests: c5yx (queue only), am9j (rebase, a retry of tw3v, depending on c5yx) and qvqq (return to producer and thrash stop). In am9j the the person running Athena also made the critic's open records ruling: a conflicting earlier commit is carried as records only. The scope guard's pause was overridden, and the design ruling and the split were done by the the person running Athena, not Athena.
cause: Athena accepts a multi-part request as one job without a size bound. The critic can keep a 16-17 step plan through every round without forcing a split. Open design rulings (here, how to handle conflicting earlier commits in records) reach the planning rounds unresolved, because no earlier stage settles them or asks the owner. The scope guard then pauses the line on spend, but it offers no way to split the work. So the only exit is for the the person running Athena to cut the request up and decide the ruling by hand.
prevention: Add a plan-size check at the critic and at reading acceptance. A set number of plan steps, or an estimate above the producer's budget and deadline, should make Athena split the request into ordered dependent jobs itself. Any open design ruling in a plan should be raised for decision before the next planning round, not carried through the rounds. When the scope guard pauses a line after planning failures on size, it should propose the split, so the the person running Athena does not have to write it.
proposed_request: Make Athena split an oversized plan before it fails planning. (1) Set a maximum plan size, in steps and in estimated producer cost against the job's remaining budget, and make the critic return "too large, split" as a blocker above it. (2) On that verdict, have Athena propose ordered dependent child requests, each with its own acceptance criteria, and queue them. (3) Have the critic list open design rulings separately. Any ruling still open after round 1 should go to the owner or to a decision record, not be carried to the last round. (4) When the scope guard pauses a line because planning failed on size, show the proposed split in `athena status`. Acceptance: replay the plans of jobs tw3v and its earlier attempt on line f5qm; both must produce a split proposal, not a pass. Add a test where an open ruling at round 2 produces a decision request.
